Current best: config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) with validation accuracy 0.713087

Key findings from the experiments:
1. RNA-only single profile: PCA (0.485) < scvi_n200 (0.520)
2. RNA-only multiprofile: scvi_n200 + transformer (0.653) > scvi_n200 + avgpool (0.650) > scgpt + transformer (0.514)
3. Image-only single profile: resnet50 (0.208) - very poor
4. Multimodal multiprofile scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer: concat (0.688) < weighted (0.713)

So the progression shows:
- scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder (vs PCA and scgpt)
- multiprofile is much better than singleprofile
- transformer aggregation is slightly better than avgpool
- multimodal is better than rna_only
- weighted fusion is better than concat
- resnet50 image encoder is used (but image-only is very poor, suggesting the image adds value in multimodal context)

The current best is config_033 at 0.713. The remaining question is whether we can improve further.

Options to consider:
1. Try imagenet_vit_l instead of resnet50 as image encoder with the best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) → config_039
2. Try scgpt with multimodal (but scgpt was much worse than scvi_n200 in RNA-only)
3. Try other variations

The most logical next step is to test whether a better image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can improve upon resnet50 in the multimodal setting. The image-only resnet50 was very poor (0.208), but in multimodal context it still helped (0.713 vs 0.653 for RNA-only). A stronger image encoder might provide better features.

config_039: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted

This is the most natural extension of the current best (config_033) - just swapping the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l. This isolates the effect of the image encoder quality while keeping all other settings at their best-known values.

Alternatively, config_038 (concat instead of weighted) - but we already know weighted > concat from config_032 vs config_033.

I think config_039 is the best choice. It tests whether a more powerful image encoder (ViT-L pretrained on ImageNet) can further improve the multimodal model, which is the most promising direction given that the current best already leverages multimodal fusion.

This is experiment 9 of 10, so we have 1 experiment left after this. If config_039 improves, we're done. If not, we still have one more experiment to try something else. But testing the image encoder quality is the most impactful remaining question.
